## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 1978 [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_\(Australia\) "Victoria (Australia)"), Mark "Chopper" Read is an inmate at [Pentridge Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentridge_Prison "Pentridge Prison"). Keithy George, another inmate, points to a line in the yard and tells Mark not to cross the line as it marks the [Painters and Dockers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_Ship_Painters_and_Dockers_Union "Federated Ship Painters and Dockers Union") territory. The next day, Mark rushes across the line and stabs Keithy multiple times.

The Painters and Dockers put out a $10,000 [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_killing "Contract killing") on Mark. Mark conscripts Bluey Barnes and Jimmy Loughnan to help him lead a siege on the Painters and Dockers. Wanting out of the suicide mission, Jimmy [shanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiv_\(weapon\) "Shiv (weapon)") Mark. Jimmy slashes his own arm so that he can claim self-defense. Mark recovers and is returned to a separate cell from Bluey and Jimmy. It is revealed that Mark is serving a 16\+1⁄2\-year sentence for the [attempted abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidnapping "Kidnapping") of a judge in order to give Jimmy Loughnan freedom.

Mark meets with the prison board to negotiate a change of prisons for security. The board declines, so Mark has his ears cut off so that he can relocate to a mental health wing where he serves the remainder of his sentence.

When Mark is released from prison, he reunites with his old girlfriend Tanya. While out at a club, Mark flies into a jealous rage and fires several shots with a handgun. Back at Tanya's house, Mark finds her on the phone with Neville Bartos ([Vince Colosimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Colosimo "Vince Colosimo")). He physically abuses both Tanya and her mother. Mark goes to Neville's house and learns that Neville supplies most of the 'goey' (amphetamine/ 'speed') to the western suburbs of Melbourne and is very wealthy. When Neville refuses to give Mark money, Mark shoots him in the abdomen.

Mark goes to Jimmy Loughnan's apartment that he shares with his pregnant fiancée, Mandy, and their young daughter. Mark reveals that he's working for the police, stating that he has a green light to shoot criminals and that he shot Neville. Mark tells Jimmy that he heard about the contracts out on his life and that Jimmy was meant to do them, and then holds a gun to Jimmy's head. Eventually, Mark apologises and gives money to Jimmy.

In a car park at the Bojangles, Sammy the Turk, another affiliate, states that he wants to show Mark something. Mark produces a [sawed-off .410 shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawed-off_shotgun "Sawed-off shotgun") and after a brief argument, Mark shoots him in the eye. Mandy witnesses the murder from behind a parked car and tells Jimmy.

Mandy turns [crown witness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_state's_evidence "Turn state's evidence") against Mark for the murder of Sammy the Turk. It's revealed that Sammy took Mark out to the car park for Jimmy to cash in on the contract against Mark, but unknowingly took him to the wrong car park. Mark beats the murder charge but is convicted of [malicious wounding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grievous_bodily_harm "Grievous bodily harm") of Neville Bartos, and is sentenced to 5 years.

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Read himself suggested that Bana play him, after seeing the actor in the sketch comedy series *[Full Frontal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_Frontal_\(Australian_TV_series\) "Full Frontal (Australian TV series)")*. Bana spent two days living with Read to help him practice for the role, and many of Read's friends, enemies, and old associates were interviewed. Several of Bana's meetings with Read can be viewed in the [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") special features.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

The biggest production difficulty was being allowed to use the [Pentridge Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentridge_Prison "Pentridge Prison") in [Coburg, Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coburg,_Victoria "Coburg, Victoria"), for the shooting. The prison was being closed down and while the negotiations were underway, the funding for production was delayed. This put off the start of the shoot. Some [extras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_\(actor\) "Extra (actor)") were hired from former inmates and tattoo parlours.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

To show the sterility of the prison and to contrast it with the world that Chopper encounters after leaving prison 16 years later, the production was split into two.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The first part, filmed at the H Division of Pentridge Prison, one of the actual prisons that Chopper frequented, was as plain and sterile as could be and all the scenes in the second part, taking place in 1986, were overly coloured[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) to achieve a [paranoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paranoia "Paranoia") and [agoraphobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agoraphobia "Agoraphobia") atmosphere called "visual overload" by the director Andrew Dominik. This was attained by lighting, choice of [film stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_stock "Film stock") used, and colours chosen for set decoration. Part one of the production ran from 3 May until 26 May with part two continuing from 28 June until 21 July 2000\. The month-long break enabled Bana to put on the extra weight necessary to play the older Read.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

*Chopper* was received with positive reviews. Review-based rating site [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gave the film a 76% "fresh" rating from 80 critics, with its critical consensus stating "Eric Bana's performance as the charming but twisted Chopper is the highlight of this disturbing portrait of Australia's notorious author/criminal."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_average "Weighted average"), assigned the film a score of 68 out of 100, based on 26 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the *[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")* gave the film 3 stars out of 4, praising Bana for his performance, saying, "He has a quality no acting school can teach and few actors can match."[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) [Margaret Pomeranz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Pomeranz "Margaret Pomeranz") for [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service") gave the film four-and-a-half stars out of five, commenting that what Dominik "achieved is extraordinary." [David Stratton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Stratton "David Stratton"), in the same review, remarked "There's no doubting the intelligence of Andrew Dominik's direction" and declared Bana's performance as "astonishing."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

Read later praised Bana's performance on the *[20 to 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20_to_1 "20 to 1")* episode *Great Aussie Films*, where *Chopper* came 17th.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")\]

*Chopper* was given a wide release in Australia on 3 August 2000 appearing on 132 screens, despite its R (over 18) rating. It grossed A$300,000 in previews before becoming the [number one film in Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2000_box_office_number-one_films_in_Australia "List of 2000 box office number-one films in Australia"), knocking Mel Gibson helmer, The Patriot, from the top spot, with a gross of A$1.8 million in its opening week.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It went on to gross A$5,912,119 in Australia[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) It grossed US$0.2 million in the United States and Canada and US$0.3 million in other territories for a worldwide total of A$6.8 million.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Numbers-3) It was released on 8 September 2000 in Canada, appearing in the Discovery section of the [Toronto International Film Festival 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2000 Toronto International Film Festival").

*Chopper* received a limited re-release in Australian cinemas on 21 August 2025 for its 25th Anniversary. This featured some additional behind the scenes footage.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

Chopper

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/6e/Choppermovie.jpg/250px-Choppermovie.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Choppermovie.jpg) Theatrical release poster

***Chopper*** is a 2000 Australian [crime drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_film "Crime film") written and directed by [Andrew Dominik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Dominik "Andrew Dominik"), in his feature directorial debut, based on the [autobiographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiography "Autobiography") books by the criminal turned author [Mark "Chopper" Read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_"Chopper"_Read "Mark \"Chopper\" Read"). The film stars [Eric Bana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Bana "Eric Bana") as the title character and co-stars [Vince Colosimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Colosimo "Vince Colosimo"), [Simon Lyndon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Lyndon "Simon Lyndon"), [Kate Beahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Beahan "Kate Beahan") and [David Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Field_\(actor\) "David Field (actor)"). The film follows Read's life and time in prison. The film grossed $6.8 million worldwide and received positive reviews.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Numbers-3) It has since garnered a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 1978 [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_\(Australia\) "Victoria (Australia)"), Mark "Chopper" Read is an inmate at [Pentridge Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentridge_Prison "Pentridge Prison"). Keithy George, another inmate, points to a line in the yard and tells Mark not to cross the line as it marks the [Painters and Dockers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_Ship_Painters_and_Dockers_Union "Federated Ship Painters and Dockers Union") territory. The next day, Mark rushes across the line and stabs Keithy multiple times.

The Painters and Dockers put out a $10,000 [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_killing "Contract killing") on Mark. Mark conscripts Bluey Barnes and Jimmy Loughnan to help him lead a siege on the Painters and Dockers. Wanting out of the suicide mission, Jimmy [shanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiv_\(weapon\) "Shiv (weapon)") Mark. Jimmy slashes his own arm so that he can claim self-defense. Mark recovers and is returned to a separate cell from Bluey and Jimmy. It is revealed that Mark is serving a 16\+1⁄2\-year sentence for the [attempted abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidnapping "Kidnapping") of a judge in order to give Jimmy Loughnan freedom.

Mark meets with the prison board to negotiate a change of prisons for security. The board declines, so Mark has his ears cut off so that he can relocate to a mental health wing where he serves the remainder of his sentence.

When Mark is released from prison, he reunites with his old girlfriend Tanya. While out at a club, Mark flies into a jealous rage and fires several shots with a handgun. Back at Tanya's house, Mark finds her on the phone with Neville Bartos ([Vince Colosimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Colosimo "Vince Colosimo")). He physically abuses both Tanya and her mother. Mark goes to Neville's house and learns that Neville supplies most of the 'goey' (amphetamine/ 'speed') to the western suburbs of Melbourne and is very wealthy. When Neville refuses to give Mark money, Mark shoots him in the abdomen.

Mark goes to Jimmy Loughnan's apartment that he shares with his pregnant fiancée, Mandy, and their young daughter. Mark reveals that he's working for the police, stating that he has a green light to shoot criminals and that he shot Neville. Mark tells Jimmy that he heard about the contracts out on his life and that Jimmy was meant to do them, and then holds a gun to Jimmy's head. Eventually, Mark apologises and gives money to Jimmy.

In a car park at the Bojangles, Sammy the Turk, another affiliate, states that he wants to show Mark something. Mark produces a [sawed-off .410 shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawed-off_shotgun "Sawed-off shotgun") and after a brief argument, Mark shoots him in the eye. Mandy witnesses the murder from behind a parked car and tells Jimmy.

Mandy turns [crown witness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_state's_evidence "Turn state's evidence") against Mark for the murder of Sammy the Turk. It's revealed that Sammy took Mark out to the car park for Jimmy to cash in on the contract against Mark, but unknowingly took him to the wrong car park. Mark beats the murder charge but is convicted of [malicious wounding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grievous_bodily_harm "Grievous bodily harm") of Neville Bartos, and is sentenced to 5 years.

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Read himself suggested that Bana play him, after seeing the actor in the sketch comedy series *[Full Frontal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_Frontal_\(Australian_TV_series\) "Full Frontal (Australian TV series)")*. Bana spent two days living with Read to help him practice for the role, and many of Read's friends, enemies, and old associates were interviewed. Several of Bana's meetings with Read can be viewed in the [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") special features.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

The biggest production difficulty was being allowed to use the [Pentridge Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentridge_Prison "Pentridge Prison") in [Coburg, Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coburg,_Victoria "Coburg, Victoria"), for the shooting. The prison was being closed down and while the negotiations were underway, the funding for production was delayed. This put off the start of the shoot. Some [extras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_\(actor\) "Extra (actor)") were hired from former inmates and tattoo parlours.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

To show the sterility of the prison and to contrast it with the world that Chopper encounters after leaving prison 16 years later, the production was split into two.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The first part, filmed at the H Division of Pentridge Prison, one of the actual prisons that Chopper frequented, was as plain and sterile as could be and all the scenes in the second part, taking place in 1986, were overly coloured[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) to achieve a [paranoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paranoia "Paranoia") and [agoraphobic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agoraphobia "Agoraphobia") atmosphere called "visual overload" by the director Andrew Dominik. This was attained by lighting, choice of [film stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_stock "Film stock") used, and colours chosen for set decoration. Part one of the production ran from 3 May until 26 May with part two continuing from 28 June until 21 July 2000\. The month-long break enabled Bana to put on the extra weight necessary to play the older Read.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

*Chopper* was received with positive reviews. Review-based rating site [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gave the film a 76% "fresh" rating from 80 critics, with its critical consensus stating "Eric Bana's performance as the charming but twisted Chopper is the highlight of this disturbing portrait of Australia's notorious author/criminal."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_average "Weighted average"), assigned the film a score of 68 out of 100, based on 26 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the *[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")* gave the film 3 stars out of 4, praising Bana for his performance, saying, "He has a quality no acting school can teach and few actors can match."[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) [Margaret Pomeranz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Pomeranz "Margaret Pomeranz") for [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service") gave the film four-and-a-half stars out of five, commenting that what Dominik "achieved is extraordinary." [David Stratton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Stratton "David Stratton"), in the same review, remarked "There's no doubting the intelligence of Andrew Dominik's direction" and declared Bana's performance as "astonishing."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

Read later praised Bana's performance on the *[20 to 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20_to_1 "20 to 1")* episode *Great Aussie Films*, where *Chopper* came 17th.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")\]

*Chopper* was given a wide release in Australia on 3 August 2000 appearing on 132 screens, despite its R (over 18) rating. It grossed A$300,000 in previews before becoming the [number one film in Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2000_box_office_number-one_films_in_Australia "List of 2000 box office number-one films in Australia"), knocking Mel Gibson helmer, The Patriot, from the top spot, with a gross of A$1.8 million in its opening week.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It went on to gross A$5,912,119 in Australia[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) It grossed US$0.2 million in the United States and Canada and US$0.3 million in other territories for a worldwide total of A$6.8 million.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Numbers-3) It was released on 8 September 2000 in Canada, appearing in the Discovery section of the [Toronto International Film Festival 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2000 Toronto International Film Festival").

*Chopper* received a limited re-release in Australian cinemas on 21 August 2025 for its 25th Anniversary. This featured some additional behind the scenes footage.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

## Home video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Chopper_\(film\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Home video")\]

In Australia, the film was released on DVD and VHS in 2001 by [20th Century Fox Home Entertainment South Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox_Home_Entertainment "20th Century Fox Home Entertainment").[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) For the United States, it received a VHS release in 2001 through [First Look Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Look_Pictures "First Look Pictures"). In 2020, a 20th anniversary edition Blu-Ray was released in Australia by [Madman Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madman_Entertainment "Madman Entertainment").[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)
